A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed from DeGSS to PD2GS. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-E support comparison, with clear correspondence between the original methods and experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and joint-estimation experiments on PartNet-Mobility and RS-Art, together with refinement and interaction-state ablations in Tables 1-6.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds original interpolation, camera-pose robustness, five-part modeling, timing, and component-level evaluations.

M1.justification: The latent-conditioned Gaussian deformation, loss, trajectory clustering, VLM part counting, SAM prompting, recursive splitting, and mesh/joint estimation procedures remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A. The renaming and revised visibility-threshold setting do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: The original PartNet-Mobility and RS-Art coverage remains. v2 adds evaluations with five movable parts (Table 6), cluttered real-scene RS-Art captures, and the PARIS real-scene benchmark (Figure 15 and Appendix D.3). These extend articulation complexity and capture conditions beyond v1's evaluations.

E2.justification: The original Table 1 comparator set remains unchanged. v2 adds D-NeRF, D2NeRF, Dynamic3DGS, 4D-GS, and ArtGS to the quantitative unseen-state comparison (Table 2), NAP and SINGAPO to the generative comparison (Table 9), and SAGD as an evaluated segmentation comparator (Table 14). DTArt also joins the qualitative interpolation comparison in Figure 5.

E3.justification: The four-state, 200-image main protocol already appeared in v1 Appendix C. v2 adds two-state controls across eight categories, PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS interpolation evaluation, Gaussian-noise and COLMAP pose protocols, timing procedures, and best-of-50 input-view selection for SINGAPO. Section 3.4 also replaces tau_vis=1.2 with tuning on one or two representative instances; this reports a setting revision without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The original refinement and interaction-state ablations remain unchanged as v2 Tables 11-12. New analyses test VLM prompting alternatives, SAM segmentation against SAGD, and individual pipeline stages (Tables 13-15). Camera-pose robustness, broader two-state controls, and five-part scalability tests substantially expand the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain first-run reporting and qualitative assertions about run-to-run variation in Section 5.2. Neither adds repeated-run summaries, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new pose-noise standard deviations describe experimental perturbations, not uncertainty in performance estimates.

E6.justification: The numerical results in all six original tables are preserved: v1 Tables 1-6 correspond to v2 Tables 1, 4, 5, 7, 11, and 12. v2 adds substantial new results, including PD2GS's unseen-state PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS of 28.02/0.93/0.09 (Table 2), component-count accuracies of 100% versus 90% and 15% for alternative prompts (Table 13), and robustness, scalability, and timing results. These are newly reported evaluations, not performance gains over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1-15 and Appendix A's projection, splitting, joint-classification rule, and joint-parameter derivations are retained. Changes to latent symbols and terminology are not substantive mathematical revisions; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The contributions of self-supervised Gaussian modeling, progressive part segmentation, and RS-Art remain. v2 explicitly claims superior consistency under continuous control in the abstract and adds an introduction claim about remaining within Gaussian parameterization without incompatible geometric or physics constraints. These refine the existing contribution claims rather than introduce a different research contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations contrasting generative plausibility with instance-specific reconstruction and explaining the computational cost of deformation-based inference. It also interprets the new component and robustness results. The pose discussion calls degradation slight, although Table 8 shows axis-angle error rising from 0.40 to 10.00 under stronger noise. Appendix E largely retains its limitations, adding diffusion priors as a possible completion direction.

D1.justification: v2 adds training/inference times and explains baseline interpolation timing in Appendix D.6. It documents visibility-threshold tuning but removes the fixed value, and deletes v1's disclosure that ArticulatedGS was reimplemented using official 3DGS and the paper's description. Both versions retain the same promise to release code and datasets upon publication.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work substantially expand positioning against dynamic rendering and conditional generative articulated models. Added works include D-NeRF, D2NeRF, NAP, SINGAPO, and additional dynamic Gaussian approaches; DGD and several background references disappear. Publication updates to retained works such as ArtGS and ArticulatedGS do not constitute new citations.

P1.justification: The title and method name change, and the abstract, introduction, and related work undergo extensive rewriting. Metric explanations and experimental narratives expand, Appendix D is reorganized from three subsections into seven, and terminology and author/header information are revised. Much of the method text and Appendices A-C remains closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 adds a teaser figure, new interpolation and real-scene comparison figures, and nine new tables. Existing displays are relocated, resized, and selectively trimmed or rearranged. Table 1 drops the Manual column and adds a depth-input clarification, while the conference format substantially reflows the document.

improvement.justification: v1 supports unseen-state control mainly through qualitative examples. v2 adds quantitative comparisons with dynamic rendering methods (Table 2), broader two-state controls (Table 3), and targeted validation of prompting and segmentation (Tables 13-15), substantially strengthening evidence for central claims. These gains outweigh the limited loss of implementation disclosure and overstated pose-robustness interpretation. First-run reporting without uncertainty remains an unresolved weakness.
